A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the majority of the survey groups support the explicit use of priority scoring systems for elective health care and agree that clinical factors should be the most influential in determining priority.
the public and professionals are in agreement that clinical need, rather than waiting time, should be used to determine patient priority.
there is a clear need for the explicit rationing of waiting lists.
The main takeaway from our work is that
there is a need to ensure that the public is informed about the rationing process, that it is seen to be fair, and that it is seen as a means of improving access to care for those in greatest need.
the NHS should consider using priority scoring systems as one means of ensuring that waiting times are not the only determinant of access to elective health services.

, in order to ensure that patients are treated in line with clinical need rather than waiting time, the NHS needs to be explicit about the factors which will determine patient priority on waiting lists.
